title: What does it mean for culture to ‘shape’ cognition?
title_zh: 文化是如何‘塑造’认知的？
abstract: Human culture and cognition vary widely across groups, but how exactly culture 'shapes' cognition remains underspecified. In this review, we outline four qualitatively different pathways by which culture can shape cognition. In this framework, culture can (i) privilege some cognitive processes, while leaving alternative processes intact; (ii) prune unused alternative processes, which are irretrievably lost; (iii) produce new cognitive processes; or (iv) have no effect on cognition at all. To illustrate the utility of this framework, we apply it to three debated effects of culture on cognitive processes, namely, visual illusions, large exact number abilities, and spatial-numerical associations. The distinctions we propose can serve to reframe long-standing debates, sharpen empirical predictions, and open new avenues of research in cognitive diversity.
abstract_zh: 人类文化在不同群体中差异巨大，但文化究竟是如何‘塑造’认知的，这一过程仍然描述不清。在本综述中，我们概述了文化通过四种定性不同的途径塑造认知的可能路径。在此框架下，文化可以（i）优先考虑某些认知过程，同时保持其他过程完整；(ii) 剪除未被使用的备选过程，这些过程将不可逆转地丢失；(iii) 产生新的认知过程；或 (iv) 对认知产生完全无效应。为了说明该框架的实用性，我们将其应用于三种关于文化对认知过程影响的争议话题，即视觉错觉、大精确数能力以及空间-数字关联。我们提出的区别可以用于重新框定长期的争论，细化实验预测，并为认知多样性的研究开辟新途径。
